newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African rand at critical technical juncture.
newsitem.headline: South African rand at critical technical juncture.

text.p: The rand was poised at a critical technical juncture in early Thursday afternoon trade as continuing importer demand pushed the currency to its weakest level since August 27.
At 1040 GMT, the rand was trading at 4.5230/5280 after briefly touching a day's worst level of 4.5250 bid and from 4.5110/5160 late on Monday.
Dealers said a decisive breach above resistance around 4.5225 could signal a quick move to the 4.55 level.
"It's at its critical area (of) 4.5250," said Boyde Stafne, technical analyst at UAL Merchant Bank.
"If it breaks here it is likely we will see it two cents higher to 4.5450. After that, it's 4.57. Above there you are looking at the 4.60 area," Stafne said.
The rand's all-time low of 4.59 bid on the dollar was registered on August 19. Since then, the currency has stabilised in a 4.48 to 4.52 range.

"It has been under some short-term pressure the whole week and so this is not unexpected," Stafne said. "Longer-term technicals are still pointing to a temporary high in the dollar, and a key level which we haven't seen is the 4.61 to 4.65 area."
Dealers said there was a supply of dollars at the weaker levels which could help resistance hold.
"We've seen some export dollars coming in and there is talk that the Reserve Bank is offering, although we haven't seen him (the Bank)," a dealer said.
Officials at the central bank were not available for comment.
Should resistance hold until the weekend, another trader said the rand would resume its recent stronger trend and gradually retrace back to support at 4.48.
Stafne added that a breach of key resistance levels was unlikely to herald another long-term run on the rand.
"Its more of a short-term play," he said.
The rand has tumbled from 3.65 against the dollar since mid-February.
